While it's true that some of the religious and right wing parties target a very nationalist and anti-foreigner base of voters, my feeling is that the racism you describe is not a political thing. I had the opportunity to talk with a שס appointed member of piba this month and he was extremely sympathetic to our application and even offered to help. I also saw this group's admins mention the current piba general director, also a שס appointment, is also commited to improving the visa process and some of these improvements are already in effect.
Also, I've heard of racism towards foreigners, and sometimes citizens, that are dark skinned by apartment owners, most of which weren't religious and would often identify themselves as liberal, left wing and anti religious.
It sucks, but I guess Israel is so isolated that many people have superstitions and biases that they aren't even aware of because they rarely confront them
